question: A user asks Claude to research mode-style investigate an emerging technical standard, but Claude answers immediately from general knowledge without doing multiple searches. What is the most likely reason research mode did not activate?
options: A) Web search was not enabled, or the user did not explicitly prompt Claude for research, so it fell back to a normal response.
B) Research mode only works when the query is phrased as a single yes-or-no question, so Claude defaults to general knowledge without initiating research.
C) Research mode was permanently removed from Claude.ai and replaced entirely by Projects; all multi-step research now happens within project setups.
D) The user's account tier does not support any form of web-connected search, regardless of plan, so Claude cannot initiate research mode when requested.
correct_answers: A) Web search was not enabled, or the user did not explicitly prompt Claude for research, so it fell back to a normal response.
explanations: Correct. Research mode requires web search to be enabled, and if the user does not explicitly prompt Claude to use research capabilities, it may fall back to a normal response. This explains why Claude answered from general knowledge without performing multiple searches.
Incorrect. Research mode is designed for open-ended, multi-faceted investigative queries, not limited to yes-or-no questions. Query phrasing does not determine whether research mode initiates.

Incorrect. Research mode is still available on Claude.ai and has not been replaced by Projects. They are separate features designed for different use cases, so research mode remains a distinct capability.

Incorrect. Research mode is supported on certain paid account tiers, so it is not true that no tier supports web-connected search. The scenario does not provide account details, and the feature is not universally unavailable.
